report.source_text: Computed tomography carotid and circle of Willis angiography was undertaken to assist in surgical planning (see Figure 1). This confirmed a mixed, ulcerated plaque and revealed a persistent left hypoglossal artery originating from the left ICA 3.7 cm from its origin, ascending posterior to the ICA. This was the dominant supply to the posterior circulation with hypoplastic vertebral arteries bilaterally. The small-calibre right vertebral artery communicated with the basilar artery while the left terminated as the posterior inferior cerebellar artery.

clinician.final_diagnosis: PPHA that presented with symptoms of both anterior and posterior circulation
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old male presented with intermittent visual disturbances and left eye amaurosis fugax. Initial workup included cerebral angiography (CTA) which revealed a mixed, ulcerated plaque, a persistent left hypoglossal artery (PPHA) originating from the left ICA and serving as the dominant supply to the posterior circulation, and bilateral hypoplastic vertebral arteries. Brain MRI confirmed this aberrant anatomy and showed old and subacute infarcts in the left frontal, parietal-occipital, and cerebellar regions. Carotid Doppler ultrasound demonstrated >90% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery, which was confirmed intraoperatively as a near-occlusive soft hemorrhagic plaque. The patient underwent left carotid endarterectomy (CEA) with a Braun polyurethane patch. No neurological deterioration was observed during surgery, and post-operative analgesia was satisfactory.

Cerebral angiography (CTA) confirmed a mixed, ulcerated plaque and revealed a persistent left hypoglossal artery originating from the left ICA, which was the dominant supply to the posterior circulation, along with bilateral hypoplastic vertebral arteries.

Brain MRI confirmed the aberrant anatomy and showed old and subacute infarcts in the left frontal, parietal-occipital, and cerebellar regions, supporting both anterior and posterior circulation involvement.
Carotid Doppler ultrasound demonstrated >90% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery, which was addressed by left carotid endarterectomy.
No neurological deterioration was observed during surgery, and post-operative analgesia was satisfactory.
